title: AI System for an Air-Gapped Environment
subtitle: Run and maintain useful document AI inside a restricted enclave, with controlled artifacts, local identity and tested recovery.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Boundary and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Name what the air gap protects, the riskiest assumption and who operates the system at 2 a.m.

practice_prompts.label: Fixed-pool sizing
practice_prompts.hint: Run the replica formula and say which request-mix lever you pull when it exceeds the pool.

practice_prompts.label: Release admission and failure policy
practice_prompts.hint: Trace a bundle from build to promotion and say where a missing package or bad signature stops it.

practice_prompts.label: Rollout, metrics and ownership
practice_prompts.hint: Give the four phases, the go/no-go gates, the rollback triggers and a locally checkable success metric.

rubric: States the outcome line and treats the network, artifact, identity and audit boundaries as the design, not a firewall setting.
Runs the replica formula against the fixed GPU pool and challenges the request mix instead of asking for hardware.
Places signing and the transfer staging zone as the only bridge and names the offline registry as system of record.
Fails closed on a missing transitive package or bad signature, keeps evidence, leaves the running release untouched and adds a closure preflight.
Assigns each failure a policy (fail closed, degrade, queue, human) and keeps every observability path local.
Versions model and index as a compatible pair and admits the HMAC sketches are not a production verifier.
Rolls out through identical staging, a rehearsed transfer, a one-node canary and a tested rollback bundle with named owners.
Measures analyst turnaround from inside the enclave, separate from install, signature and saturation health.

editorial_review.evidence: Compared all 46 captured sections of the 15 Nov 2026 air-gapped capture against the earlier draft paragraph by paragraph. The draft had compressed the source heavily: it dropped the blast-radius section, the five-bucket failure taxonomy, the six technical-health metrics with calculations and alert rules, the risk register mitigations and triggers, the go/no-go gates and rollback triggers, the core-product standardisation category, the six weak-answer repairs, the answer-key evaluation table, the worksheet candidate scorecard, the 50-minute block contents, the piece-by-piece verifier walkthrough and the third SignatureError test, and it gave the three section-4 figures one shared caption. Those are restored in the walkthrough (new step 8 for metrics and ownership), deep dives and Practice; the six architecture-changing questions now say what each answer changes, and the question-tree, happy-path and failure-overlay figures each sit beside their own explanation. Practice grew from six to sixteen reveals covering every worksheet section, the four follow-ups, the mandatory drill, the 477 challenge, the dashboard question, weak/average/strong answers and the spoken summaries; the implementation-exercise answer is labelled authored. Added caveats are labelled: HMAC is symmetric, VerifiedManifest is only shallowly frozen, ValidationError is unused and both sketches do not prove transitive closure. No RAG-specific material from the reference case was transplanted. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): sketch 2's comment 'Validate the closure of the bundle' over a loop that only hashes listed artifacts → comment now reads 'Verify every listed artifact is present and unaltered', and the prose says closure needs its own preflight; the 10x ceiling 'about 4,760' → stated as 400,000 / 84 = 4,761.9, rounded up to 4,762 replicas, without commentary on the source's rounding.
